title: Ridge paths, soft thresholding, and ISTA versus FISTA
brief: Compute the whole ridge path from one SVD, derive soft thresholding as a proximal operator, and watch FISTA outrun ISTA on an ill-conditioned lasso.
hints: ridge_closed_form is one linear solve: (X^T X + lambda I) w = X^T y. Use numpy.linalg.solve, not an explicit matrix inverse.
ridge_svd_path only needs U^T y computed once; for each lambda, scale it by s / (s**2 + lambda) and rotate back through V^T, so the whole path costs one SVD plus a handful of vector operations.
effective_degrees_of_freedom is sum(s**2 / (s**2 + lambda)); when lambda is an array, return one degrees-of-freedom value per entry.
soft_threshold(x, thresh) is sign(x) * max(|x| - thresh, 0), applied elementwise; it is exactly the proximal operator of thresh * |.|.
ista and fista should both return (w, history), where history[k] is the lasso objective 0.5 * ||Xw - y||^2 + lambda * ||w||_1 after k steps, so the checks can compare convergence speed directly.

fista's momentum uses t_{k+1} = (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 t_k^2)) / 2 starting from t_0 = 1, and extrapolates z_{k+1} = w_{k+1} + ((t_k - 1) / t_{k+1}) * (w_{k+1} - w_k); the gradient step in fista is taken at z, not at w.
